writeup: TIC 401936263 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.2010 days. TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing a 5.79% dimming of the star's light, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 271.2 in the automated search. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal at the target's location with a peak signal-to-noise of 82.3, though the centroid offset measured 1.3 arcsec from the target itself. No secondary eclipse was detected in the data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The automated pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned it a score of 0.52, and the light curve passed all data quality checks without flags or issues.
